opts.B: Include few-shot examples showing the assistant correctly acknowledging and applying preference changes in responses.
opts.C: Maintain a structured state object with current preferences, update it on changes, and include it in each request.
opts.D: Implement conversation pruning to remove turns containing outdated preferences, ensuring only current ones remain in context.

exam2.q:
After deploying automated code review, developers report that approximately 35% of flagged findings are false positives falling into consistent patterns: style suggestions contradicting team conventions, security warnings for patterns safe in your deployment context, and performance suggestions that would degrade your specific use case. You want to reduce false positives while maintaining the ability to catch genuine issues.

Which approach best enables the model to generalize its judgment to novel code patterns it hasn't seen before?

opts.A: Include few-shot examples in your prompt showing annotated code snippets that distinguish acceptable patterns from genuine issues in each category.
opts.B: Create a comprehensive written specification of all patterns that should not be flagged, then include this full documentation in the system prompt.
opts.C: Add instructions to your system prompt to "be conservative," "only flag definite issues," and "consider that some patterns may be intentional."
opts.D: Implement post-processing that uses keyword matching to filter out findings containing terms like "convention," "context-dependent," or "trade-off."

exam2.q:
You are setting up a non-interactive automated code review pipeline using Claude Code. You want Claude to analyze a pulled Git diff (git diff) against the main branch and apply a custom set of code review instructions. However, you notice that when you run the pipeline, Claude only looks at the raw diff text itself and completely stops using its file-reading or code navigation tools. As a result, it fails to inspect the broader codebase repository context, which is critical because the diff modifies a core function called by many other external modules.

Which change to the CLI invocation will cause Claude to read related files in the repository while still successfully applying your custom review instructions?

opts.A: Keep --system-prompt and add --allowedTools "Read, Glob, Grep" so that the non-interactive mode permits file system tools that it otherwise disables.
opts.B: Remove --system-prompt entirely and place the review instructions in a CLAUDE.md file at the repo root, since --system-prompt is incompatible with tool use under -p.
opts.C: Stop piping the diff via stdin and instead embed the diff contents inside the prompt string, so Claude Code treats the invocation as an agentic session rather than a stream-processing one.
opts.D: Replace --system-prompt with --append-system-prompt so your review instructions are added to Claude Code's default prompt instead of overwriting the built-in guidance for using file-reading and code navigation tools.

exam2.q:
Your development team is using Claude Code to automate test generation across a large codebase. However, developers are frequently rejecting the generated test suites because Claude creates a high volume of trivial assertions or tests that merely maximize line coverage without validating meaningful behavioral logic or edge cases. You want to guide Claude to generate high-quality, production-ready tests directly without introducing high latency or modifying the core pipeline script.

Which strategy best ensures that high-quality, meaningful tests are generated in the first place?

opts.A: Add post-generation coverage analysis that automatically filters out any generated test that doesn't increase line coverage beyond what existing tests provide.
opts.B: Restrict test generation to directories where historical quality metrics show higher acceptance rates, disabling it for areas where generated tests consistently require heavy editing.
opts.C: Implement a two-phase generation where a second Claude call scores each test against quality criteria, filtering out low-scoring tests before presenting results to developers.
opts.D: Document testing standards in CLAUDE.md including valuable test criteria, available fixtures with intended use cases, and examples distinguishing meaningful behavioral tests from trivial assertions.

exam2.q:
Your music discovery assistant should consistently maintain an enthusiastic tone, explain its reasoning for each recommendation, and ask clarifying questions to better understand user preferences. You want this behavior to persist reliably across all user interactions.

Where should you define these behavioral guidelines?

opts.A: In the first assistant message, instructing Claude to follow these guidelines going forward
opts.B: In environmental variables that your application passes to the API client
opts.C: In the system prompt
opts.D: Prepended to each user message before sending to the API

exam2.q:
Your team is configuring MCP servers in Claude Code. You want to add a shared venue lookup server that all team members should have access to, and you personally want to add an experimental music playlist server that only you are testing.

Which configuration approach correctly applies MCP server scopes?

opts.A: Add venue server to ~/.claude.json and playlist server to .mcp.json
opts.B: Add both servers to your local ~/.claude.json
opts.C: Add venue server to .mcp.json and playlist server to ~/.claude.json
opts.D: Add both servers to the project-level .mcp.json file

exam2.q:
The coordinator provides detailed step-by-step instructions to the web search subagent, specifying exact search queries, source priorities, and date filters. Production monitoring reveals three issues:
1) the subagent reports "insufficient results" rather than trying alternative approaches when pre-specified searches fail;
2) research quality drops for emerging topics that don't match expected patterns;
3) the subagent rarely surfaces valuable tangential sources.
What's the most effective way to improve subagent adaptability?

opts.A: Specify research goals and quality criteria (coverage breadth, source diversity, recency) rather than procedural steps, letting the subagent determine its search strategy.
opts.B: Remove procedural details entirely, delegating with simple goals like "research X thoroughly" and relying on the subagent's general capabilities.
opts.C: Add explicit fallback directives to the detailed instructions: "If specified searches yield fewer than N results, attempt alternative query formulations before reporting failure."
opts.D: Implement a topic classification step where the coordinator categorizes requests as "well-defined" or "exploratory" and uses different instruction styles for each category.

exam2.q: When researching "renewable energy adoption," the web search agent returns recent statistics (2024: 35% adoption) while the document analysis agent extracts data from internal reports (2022: 18% adoption). The synthesis agent incorrectly flags these as contradictory sources rather than recognizing the data shows growth over time. What change would best enable the synthesis agent to correctly interpret such temporal differences?

opts.A: Require subagents to include publication or data collection dates in their structured outputs.
opts.B: Add a conflict resolution agent that automatically discards older data when newer data exists for the same metric.
opts.C: Configure the web search agent to only return results from the past 6 months.
opts.D: Instruct the synthesis agent to always treat the most recent data as authoritative and place older findings in a separate historical appendix.

exam2.q: Production reviews reveal inconsistent handling of uncertainty in final reports. Sometimes conflicting subagent findings are synthesized into a single confident statement (losing nuance), while other times reports over-hedge with excessive qualifications (becoming unhelpful). When the web search agent returns "industry analysts estimate $50B market size (methodology varies)" and the document analysis agent returns "peer-reviewed study estimates $35B (±7B, 95% CI)," the coordinator either picks one arbitrarily or produces vague statements like "the market may be $35B−$50B depending on factors." What systematic approach best addresses this?

opts.A: Configure subagents to only report findings meeting a high-confidence threshold, filtering uncertain information before it reaches the coordinator.
opts.B: Implement a confidence calibration layer that normalizes subagent uncertainty expressions to standardized probability scores (0.0-1.0), then weight-average findings by their calibrated confidence.
opts.C: Instruct the synthesis agent to structure reports with explicit sections distinguishing well-established findings from contested ones, preserving original source characterizations and methodological context.
opts.D: Add a verification subagent that cross-references findings across sources, only passing claims to synthesis that are corroborated by at least two independent sources.

exam2.q: A customer returns 4 hours after their initial session about the same billing dispute. The previous 32-turn session contains lookup_order results showing "Status: PENDING, Expected resolution: 24-48 hours." In testing, you observe that when resuming sessions with stale tool results, the agent often references the outdated data in responses (e.g., "I see your refund is still being processed") even after subsequent fresh tool calls return different information. What approach most reliably handles returning customers?

opts.A: Resume with full history but filter out previous tool_result messages before resuming, keeping only the human/assistant turns so the agent must re-fetch needed data.
opts.B: Start a new session, inject a structured summary of the previous interaction (issue type, actions taken, resolution status), then make fresh tool calls before engaging.
opts.C: Resume with full history and add a system prompt instruction telling the agent to always prefer the most recent tool results when multiple calls to the same tool exist in context.
opts.D: Resume with full history and configure the agent to automatically re-call all previously-used tools at session start to ensure data freshness.

exam2.q: After integrating a local MCP server providing code analysis tools (analyze_dependencies, find_dead_code, calculate_complexity), you verify the server is healthy and tools appear in the tools/list response. However, you observe that the agent consistently uses Grep to search for import statements instead of calling analyze_dependencies—even when users explicitly ask about "code dependencies." Examining tool definitions reveals: MCP: analyze_dependencies — "Analyzes dependency graph". Built-in: Grep — "Search file contents for a pattern using regular expressions. Returns matching lines with line numbers and surrounding context." What's the most effective approach to improve the agent's selection of MCP tools?

opts.A: Remove Grep from available tools when the MCP server is connected to eliminate functional overlap.
opts.B: Split analyze_dependencies into granular tools (list_imports, resolve_transitive_deps, detect_circular_deps) so each has a focused purpose less likely to overlap with Grep.
opts.C: Add routing instructions to the system prompt specifying that dependency-related questions should use MCP tools rather than Grep.
opts.D: Expand MCP tool descriptions to detail capabilities and outputs—e.g., "Builds dependency graph showing direct imports, transitive dependencies, and cycles."

exam2.q: Your codebase exploration tool stores session IDs to allow engineers to continue investigations across work sessions. An engineer spent an hour yesterday analyzing a legacy authentication module, building context about its architecture and dependencies. They want to continue today. The session ID is valid, but version control shows 3 of the 12 files the agent previously read were modified overnight by a teammate's merge. What approach best balances efficiency and accuracy?

opts.A: Resume the session and immediately have the agent re-read all 12 previously analyzed files
opts.B: Start a fresh session to ensure the agent works with current codebase state without stale assumptions
opts.C: Resume the session and inform the agent which specific files changed for targeted re-analysis
opts.D: Resume the session without informing the agent about the changed files

exam2.q: During testing, you observe that in extended exploration sessions (30+ minutes), the agent starts giving inconsistent answers about code structure it discussed earlier. Engineers report having to repeat context about modules they've already explored. What's the most effective approach to address this?

opts.A: Have the agent maintain a scratchpad file that records key findings, referencing it for subsequent questions.
opts.B: Switch to a higher-capacity model tier to provide more context window space for accumulated exploration data.
opts.C: Implement automatic context clearing every 15 minutes to ensure the agent starts with fresh, uncontaminated context.
opts.D: Create summaries of all source files before exploration begins, loading only these compressed representations into context.

exam2.q: A user is expanding the research system beyond its single web search agent by adding specialized data sources. They add a financial API agent that returns structured JSON with margins and growth rates; a news monitoring agent that returns prose summaries of recent developments; and a patent analysis agent that returns structured lists of technology. The synthesis agent combines these into executive briefings. Currently, it converts everything to bullet points, causing financial comparisons to lose tabular clarity and news summaries to lose narrative flow. What change would most improve briefing quality?

opts.A: Update the synthesis agent to render each content type appropriately—financial data as tables, news as prose, and technical lists as structured points.
opts.B: Add a format conversion layer between subagents and synthesis that transforms all outputs to a common intermediate representation (such as Markdown) to facilitate more flexible rendering.
opts.C: Standardize all subagent outputs to JSON with fields for every data type to ensure programmatic consistency across the pipeline.
opts.D: Standardize all subagent outputs to prose summaries with a uniform character to maintain a consistent executive voice regardless of the source material.

exam2.q: Your agentic loop calls the Messages API and branches on `stop_reason`. It handles `tool_use` by executing tools and treats every other value as "the model is done." In production, some final answers to users end mid-sentence. What is the most likely cause and fix?

opts.A: The model is refusing the request; add a retry with a higher temperature.
opts.B: Responses are stopping with `max_tokens`; handle that value explicitly by raising the limit or continuing the generation instead of treating it as a finished answer.
opts.C: The tool results are too long; truncate every tool result to 500 characters.
opts.D: The system prompt is too long; move instructions into the first user message.

exam2.q: A team builds a two-stage pipeline: one call drafts a technical summary, then a second call critiques the draft against a written rubric and returns specific feedback. The draft is revised and re-critiqued until the rubric passes or three rounds elapse. Which workflow pattern is this?

opts.A: Routing
opts.B: Parallelization (voting)
opts.C: Evaluator-optimizer
opts.D: Orchestrator-workers

exam2.q: According to Anthropic's guidance, what distinguishes a "workflow" from an "agent"?

opts.A: Workflows use tools; agents do not.
opts.B: Workflows orchestrate LLMs and tools through predefined code paths; agents dynamically direct their own process and tool usage.
opts.C: Agents always run multiple models in parallel; workflows use a single model.
opts.D: Workflows require fine-tuned models; agents use base models with prompts.

exam2.q: Your support agent must always call `lookup_customer` as its very first action, then choose freely among the remaining tools for the rest of the conversation. How should you configure `tool_choice`?

opts.A: Set `tool_choice` to `{"type": "any"}` for every request.
opts.B: Set `tool_choice` to `{"type": "none"}` on the first request and `auto` afterwards.
opts.C: Remove all tools except `lookup_customer` for the whole session.
opts.D: Set `tool_choice` to `{"type": "tool", "name": "lookup_customer"}` on the first request, then switch to `{"type": "auto"}` for subsequent requests.

exam2.q: When you force a specific tool with `tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "extract_invoice"}`, what happens to the text the model would normally write before the tool call?

opts.A: The model still writes a full chain-of-thought explanation before the tool_use block.
opts.B: The request fails unless you also set `stream: true`.
opts.C: The response goes straight to the tool_use block; the model does not emit natural-language text before it, even if asked to.
opts.D: The model writes text first and calls the tool only in the next turn.

exam2.q: Your repository's `.mcp.json` registers a project MCP server that needs an API token. The file must be committed so the whole team gets the server, but the token must never enter version control. What is the correct approach?

opts.A: Reference the token with environment-variable expansion, e.g. `"Authorization": "Bearer ${API_TOKEN}"`, and have each developer set `API_TOKEN` locally.
opts.B: Commit the token in `.mcp.json` and make the repository private.
opts.C: Keep `.mcp.json` out of git and email the file to each new developer.
opts.D: Hard-code the token into the MCP server's source code instead of the config file.

exam2.q: A CI job runs `claude -p` to review pull requests. For one pipeline you want Claude to be able to read and edit files but never run `Bash`, regardless of what the project settings allow. Which is the most direct, reliable control?

opts.A: Add "Never use Bash" to CLAUDE.md.
opts.B: Pass `--disallowedTools "Bash"` on the command line for that job.
opts.C: Put a PostToolUse hook that logs Bash usage after it happens.
opts.D: Lower the model's temperature so it prefers safer tools.

exam2.q: A CI script runs `claude -p "..." --output-format json` and must record how much each run cost and pass Claude's final answer to the next step. What should the script do?

opts.A: Parse the JSON result object and read its fields, such as the final `result` text and the run's cost (`total_cost_usd`).
opts.B: Ask Claude in the prompt to print its own cost estimate at the end of the answer.
opts.C: Scrape the human-readable terminal output with regular expressions.
opts.D: Call the billing console API after every run to compute the cost.

exam2.q: Your support agent must only ever call `refund_order` with the customer ID that was verified earlier in the session, even if the model passes a different ID. You want to correct the value automatically rather than block the call. Which Claude Code / Agent SDK mechanism fits best?

opts.A: A Stop hook that reviews the transcript after the session ends.
opts.B: A system-prompt reminder repeated before every turn.
opts.C: A PreToolUse hook that returns an updated tool input replacing the customer ID with the verified one before the tool runs.
opts.D: A PostToolUse hook that reverses the refund if the ID was wrong.

exam2.q: A developer is about to build a complex feature with many unknowns: edge cases, UX trade-offs, and integration constraints that they haven't thought through. What is an effective way to start with Claude Code before any code is written?

opts.A: Ask Claude to interview them with probing questions about requirements and edge cases, then write the agreed spec to a file.
opts.B: Tell Claude to implement the feature immediately and fix problems afterwards.
opts.C: Paste the entire codebase into the first prompt so Claude can infer the requirements.
opts.D: Enable auto-accept edits so Claude can explore solutions quickly.

exam2.q: You send the same 40,000-token product manual as context on thousands of requests, each followed by a different customer question. You add a `cache_control` breakpoint after the manual, but cache hits are near zero. Inspecting the requests, you see the system prompt begins with the current timestamp. What is the fix?

opts.A: Lower `max_tokens` so the cached portion fits.
opts.B: Move the variable timestamp after the cache breakpoint (or remove it) so the cached prefix is byte-identical across requests.
opts.C: Add a second `cache_control` breakpoint after each question.
opts.D: Switch to the Message Batches API, which caches automatically.

exam2.q: Your agent uses extended thinking together with tools. After executing a tool, you send back only the tool_result and drop the assistant's previous content blocks to save tokens. Requests start failing or reasoning degrades. What is required?

opts.A: Disable extended thinking whenever tools are present.
opts.B: Set `budget_tokens` higher than `max_tokens`.
opts.C: Summarize the thinking yourself and send it as a user message.
opts.D: Pass the assistant's thinking blocks back unchanged, together with the tool_use block, when you return the tool_result.

exam2.q: A contract-review prompt contains three long documents plus instructions, and Claude sometimes confuses which clause came from which document. What prompt-structuring change most directly helps?

opts.A: Wrap each document in its own descriptive XML tags (e.g. `<contract_a>…</contract_a>`) and refer to those tags in the instructions.
opts.B: Concatenate the documents without separators to save tokens.
opts.C: Put the instructions in the middle, between the second and third documents.
opts.D: Raise the temperature so Claude explores alternative readings.

exam2.q: A long Claude Code session has accumulated a lot of exploration output. You want to keep working on the same task with its key decisions preserved, but free up context. Which command fits best?

opts.A: `/clear`, because it keeps a summary of the conversation.
opts.B: Start a new terminal and re-explain the task from memory.
opts.C: `/compact`, optionally with instructions about what to keep, which replaces the history with a summary.
opts.D: Delete CLAUDE.md so it no longer consumes context.

exam2.q: A developer wants personal Claude Code instructions (their local sandbox URL and preferred test command) that apply only to them in this project and are never committed. Where should these go?

opts.A: The project's root `CLAUDE.md`.
opts.B: A `CLAUDE.local.md` file in the project root, which is meant for personal project-specific notes and kept out of git.
opts.C: The project's `.mcp.json`.
opts.D: A comment at the top of the main source file.

exam2.q: An autonomous research agent occasionally gets stuck calling the same search tool over and over, running up cost. Which safeguard most directly bounds this in production?

opts.A: Set `max_tokens` to the model maximum on every call.
opts.B: Remove the system prompt to reduce input tokens.
opts.C: Disable tool use after the first call.
opts.D: Enforce a maximum number of turns/iterations with an explicit stopping condition, and surface the stop reason to the caller.

exam2.q: You are integrating Claude Code into your CI/CD pipeline for automated code reviews. Your review jobs take 18 seconds to initialize before Claude begins analyzing code. Profiling shows the delay comes from automatically discovering hooks, MCP servers, plugins, skills, and multiple nested CLAUDE.md files throughout the monorepo. You need to reduce startup time while ensuring reviews still enforce the coding standards documented in the root-level CLAUDE.md file. What is the most effective approach?

opts.A: Replace the default prompt using --system-prompt-file ./CLAUDE.md, which bypasses default prompt assembly and loads only the project rules.
opts.B: Run in --bare mode and pass --append-system-prompt-file ./CLAUDE.md to load the required project standards explicitly while skipping automatic discovery.
opts.C: Run in --bare mode and repeat all review criteria directly in the -p prompt for every invocation.
opts.D: Keep the default initialization and add --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections to improve prompt-cache reuse across CI runners.

exam2.q: Your CI pipeline includes a release-notes generation step that classifies and summarizes approximately 200 commits at the end of each weekly release cycle. Each commit is currently sent as a separate Messages API request using a Sonnet-tier Claude model. The release notes are not needed until the following morning, giving about 12 hours of acceptable latency. Your team must reduce the per-token API cost while keeping the same model, prompts, and output quality. Which approach satisfies all these constraints?

opts.A: Issue the 200 Messages API requests concurrently because parallel execution reduces the per-token price.
opts.B: Submit the 200 requests through the Message Batches API with unique custom_id values and retrieve the results after the batch finishes.
opts.C: Concatenate all 200 commit messages into one Messages API request because reducing the number of requests always reduces token costs.
opts.D: Replace the Sonnet-tier model with a Haiku-tier model to obtain a lower per-token price.

exam2.q: Your structured data extraction system validates output with JSON schemas. Testing reveals that when source documents are missing certain specifications, the model fabricates plausible-sounding values to satisfy the schema's required fields. For example, a document mentioning only dimensions receives a fabricated "weight: 2.3 kg" in the extraction output. What schema design change most effectively addresses this hallucination behavior?

opts.A: Add explicit instructions to the prompt stating "only extract information explicitly stated in the document; use placeholder text for missing values."
opts.B: Change fields that may not exist in source documents from required to optional, allowing the model to omit them.
opts.C: Add a "confidence" field alongside each specification where the model self-reports its certainty, then filter out low-confidence extractions.
opts.D: Implement semantic validation that verifies each extracted value appears in or can be inferred from the source document text.

exam2.q: Your extraction pipeline occasionally receives responses that cannot be parsed as valid JSON, causing downstream processing failures. The current implementation prompts Claude to return JSON in the response text and then parses it. What is the most reliable approach to ensure Claude returns valid, schema-compliant structured data?

opts.A: Add explicit formatting instructions to the prompt with JSON examples, emphasizing that Claude must return only valid JSON with no surrounding text.
opts.B: Use regular expressions to locate and extract JSON from the response text, handling cases where Claude includes explanatory text around the JSON block.
opts.C: Define a tool with a JSON schema specifying the expected structure, using tool use to constrain Claude's output to schema-compliant JSON.
opts.D: Implement a retry loop that catches JSON parsing errors and re-prompts Claude with the error details, asking it to correct the malformed output.

exam2.q:
Your organization has enabled Claude's managed Code Review through the Claude GitHub App, and reviews run automatically on every pull request. Reviews average 18 findings per pull request. Developer feedback reveals three categories of unwanted noise:
1) style and formatting issues already enforced by your CI linter;
2) findings on automatically generated template code under src/gen/*;
3) rendering-helper patterns that are intentional project conventions but are flagged because they resemble common anti-patterns.
Only about four findings per pull request are genuine logic bugs. What is the most effective way to reduce this noise while preserving the detection of real issues?

opts.A: Create a REVIEW.md file at the repository root containing skip rules for CI-enforced checks and generated files, together with a verification requirement that rendering-related findings cite a specific line demonstrating incorrect behavior.
opts.B: Configure separate GitHub Actions workflow files for each code area: one for generated code with findings suppressed, one for rendering code with custom instructions, and one general workflow for everything else.
opts.C: Add custom review instructions to a GitHub Actions workflow file, using the action's prompt parameter to suppress duplicate lint findings, ignore generated template code, and impose stricter evidence requirements on rendering-related issues.
opts.D: Add detailed explanations to the project's CLAUDE.md describing intentional patterns, stating that CI handles linting, and identifying src/gen/ as automatically generated code.

exam2.q: Your team has connected a custom MCP server to Claude Code that provides DevOps workflow templates. The server exposes several MCP prompts (such as deploy_checklist and incident_response) in addition to tools. How do these MCP prompts become accessible within Claude Code?

opts.A: They are automatically prepended to every conversation as additional system-level context, influencing Claude's behavior throughout the session.
opts.B: They are added to Claude Code's tool registry alongside the server's tools, invoked automatically by the model when relevant to the task.
opts.C: They are surfaced as @-mentionable resources alongside files, fetched and attached to your message when referenced.
opts.D: They appear as slash commands (e.g., /mcp__servername__deploy_checklist) that you can invoke, with arguments passed after the command name.

exam2.q: During testing, you find that when a customer says "I need a refund for my recent purchase," the agent calls process_refund immediately, but populates the required order_id parameter with a plausible-looking but fabricated value instead of first calling lookup_order to retrieve the actual order ID. The refund call fails because the fabricated ID doesn't exist. Which change directly addresses the root cause of the agent fabricating the order_id value?

opts.A: Switch tool_choice from "auto" to "any" to force the agent to make a tool call on every turn.
opts.B: Pre-parse incoming customer messages to extract any order IDs mentioned, and inject them into the conversation context before passing to Claude.
opts.C: Update the process_refund tool description to explicitly state that order_id must be obtained from a prior lookup_order call and must never be assumed or invented.
opts.D: Add server-side validation that checks whether the order_id exists in your database before executing, returning an error to the agent if not.
